messages:
Maya: p99 spike seen in hosted API around 14:04 UTC, rolling from ~220ms -> 1.1s for a 10m window. Graph: https://grafana/redwood/d/serving/p99
infra-bot: ALERT: hosted-api.p99 above threshold (1.02s) for 8m. top affected route: /v1/generate. top hosts: gpu-pool-7a-[3..6].
Maya: anyone on call/near the runtime dashboard? I'm seeing a simultaneous jump in queue_depth and kvcache_evictions.
Sam: looking. queue_depth for pool-7a spiked to 18 (usual <3). kvcache_evictions increased x6. My local flame showed long spin in kernel_selector.cpp on auxiliary kernels.
Priya: ran a quick query: kernel_selector switched to "aux_smallseq_v2" for short sequence batches at 14:02:37. shortseq_ratio jumped from 12% -> 48% because of tenant A's request mix. command: `SELECT time, kernel FROM kernel_hist WHERE pool='7a' ORDER BY time DESC LIMIT 50;`
Eli: that matches a noisy-tenant pattern. If tenant A sent many small requests, batching heuristics may keep coalescing into small batches and priority fallback to aux kernels which have worse p95 due to prefetch overhead.
Sam: attaching quick snippet from perf top (reduced):
```
  samples  shared objects  symbol
  32.4%   libruntime.so    kernel_selector::choose_kernel
  18.1%   libruntime.so    kv_cache::evict_path
  9.7%    libnvllama.so    attention_kernels::aux_prefetch
```
Maya: ops-bot any recent config changes for rate limits or batch windows? Couldn't find deploys in the last hour.
ops-bot: No deploys. Rate-limiter config for hosted-api unchanged. Noted tenant A had a bursty increase -> 2.4x tokens/s starting 14:01 UTC; an automated quota bump for ephemeral workers was applied at 14:03 to reduce errors.
Priya: hypothesis: quota bump + burst of short requests changed runtime routing: more shortseq, kernel_selector prefers aux kernel to reduce memory but aux has higher latency when prefetch thrash occurs. kvcache eviction rate increases due to more KV churn.
Eli: can we confirm per-tenant kernel choice? I pulled: tenant A requests mapped to aux_smallseq_v2 94% of the time during spike.
Sam: quick mitigation proposal: temporarily force kernel_selector policy to prefer main_singlepass for pool-7a for 10m to measure impact. Also transiently increase kvcache size for pool-7a by +20%.
Maya: +1 to both. Sam, can you run the kernel pin? Priya, can you patch kvcache size? I'll coordinate with SRE to watch for regressions.
Sam: running: `curl -XPOST https://controlplane/api/v1/pools/7a/actions -d '{"action":"pin_kernel","kernel":"main_singlepass"}'` -> 200 OK at 14:08:12
Priya: bumped kvcache.max_items from 1.2M to 1.44M for pool-7a at 14:08:30.
infra-bot: Config change applied. Observability note: watch hosted-api.p95 and queue_depth.
Maya: p99 dropped to ~330ms within 90s. queue_depth back to 2-3. kvcache_evictions decreased. Looks like kernel choice was main lever.
Eli: still want long-term fix: adjust batching sampler to avoid amplifying small request churn; also consider kernel latency profile weight in selector when kvcache_evictions > X.
Sam: filing follow-up perf ticket and eval harness to reproduce noisy-tenant smallseq pattern. I'll include perf traces and flamegraphs.
Maya: action items: Sam -> /tickets/INF-1429 pin rollback + perf harness; Priya -> /tickets/INF-1430 kvcache autoscale rule; Eli -> /tickets/INF-1431 batching sampler tweak. I'll close once postmortem added.
ops-bot: Incident tag: hosted-p99-slabbed-4381234567. Notify: #oncall-eng-runtime, #sre. :white_check_mark:
Maya: thanks all :thumbsup:
